p: Escape rooms reward a bit of planning. Before your game starts, decide who's going to watch the clock and who'll keep hold of the bits you find, because things can get chaotic once the timer's running. Search thoroughly before you try to solve, share every find out loud, and don't spend ages hammering away at the same lock. Step back, look at what you haven't used yet, and the answer often jumps out.

Groups of mixed ages do surprisingly well. Kids are brilliant at spotting the small details adults skim past, while grown-ups tend to be good at keeping track of the bigger picture. Put them together and you've got a properly balanced team. Try not to let one loud voice take over, either. The quiet member of the group often notices the one detail everyone else missed, so give them space to speak up.

The Ram Quarter itself is worth a look. The site was home to the Ram Brewery, where beer was brewed for centuries, and the redevelopment has kept some of the old brewery buildings, giving the area plenty of character. Wandsworth Town station is close by for trains into Waterloo and Clapham Junction, making it easy to reach from across London.

For a longer day out, the Thames is just to the north, and a walk along the river towards Putney brings you to Putney Bridge and its riverside pubs, a lovely spot on a sunny afternoon. Battersea Park, with its lakes, gardens and children's zoo, is a short trip east. You can also follow the Wandle Trail, which traces the River Wandle south through a string of parks and green spaces.
